llama.raw_text: Aphids are sucking pests of tomatoes. Use nitrogen fertilizer judiciously.
llama.text: Aphids are sucking pests of tomatoes. Use nitrogen fertilizer judiciously.

llama.raw_text: Seedlings, leaves, stem, and fruits are affected. Spots appear on leaves, stems, and fruits. White blisters form in the margins of leaves. Leaves and shoots wilt. Streaks appear on stems and petioles. Small, water-soaked spots with a white halo appear on fruits. The center of the spots becomes raised, tan, and rough. Cankers develop and form cracks.

llama.raw_text: Small black spots appear on the leaf, stem, and parts that hold the leaf to the plant. Irregular, elongated lesions appear on the stem.

llama.raw_text: Small, brown, water-soaked, circular spots with a yellow halo appear on leaves. Use disease-free seed.

dropped_sentences: A white, sticky liquid comes out of the cut ends when the plant is cut and submerged in clear water.
llama.raw_text: Wilting of the plant happens quickly and completely. Lower leaves drop off before wilting. A white, sticky liquid comes out of the cut ends when the plant is cut and submerged in clear water.
llama.text: Wilting of the plant happens quickly and completely. Lower leaves drop off before wilting.

llama.raw_text: Soft tissue necrosis appears on the stem near the soil line. White, cottony, and silvery mycelial growth is visible on the affected area. Later, a white to light brown mustard-like sclerotium appears. Plants may collapse soon after infection. Use crop rotation with cereals, corn, sorghum, and millets. Remove all weeds from the field. Do not use infested farmyard manure, soil crop debris, or compost in the field. Irrigate the soil in summer and plough the field to destroy germinating sclerotia. Use Ammonium Nitrate as a fertilizer.

llama.raw_text: Seedlings rot completely before reaching the soil. Use raised beds of 15 cm height.

llama.raw_text: Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with a yellow margin appear on the leaves. Irregular leaf spots appear on the margins of the leaves. The disease appears in the vegetative phase of the plant growth before flowering.

llama.raw_text: Rhizoctonia fruit rot is the most serious disease of kharif tomatoes. To prevent the disease, keep the fruits off the soil by staking the plants. Ensure proper drainage in the field.

llama.raw_text: Younger leaves die one by one. Petiole and leaves droop and wilt.
llama.text: Younger leaves die one by one. Petiole and leaves droop and wilt.

llama.raw_text: Small circular dark brown necrotic, numerous spots appear all over the leaf lamina that is uniformly distributed on entire foliage. Sometimes clear narrow yellow halo is visible around the spots. Usually these spots are isolated but in later stage they coalesce to each other. Severely infected older leaves blight and fall down.

llama.raw_text: Rotate tomato plants with non-host crops like cereals and legumes. Do not plant tomatoes with chillies or brinjals.
llama.text: Rotate tomato plants with non-host crops like cereals and legumes. Do not plant tomatoes with chillies or brinjals.

llama.raw_text: Young larvae eat tender leaves. Mature larvae make circular holes in the leaves. Eggs hatch in 3-4 days and the first larvae eat leaves and later move to the fruit.

dropped_sentences: Black lesions appear on leaves and stems, and the entire leaf turns necrotic.
Dark brown lesions appear on fruit, and soft rot and disintegration of fruits occur.
llama.raw_text: Black lesions appear on leaves and stems, and the entire leaf turns necrotic. The lesions expand rapidly, and the leaf becomes completely dead. White spores are seen on leaves. Dark brown lesions appear on fruit, and soft rot and disintegration of fruits occur.
llama.text: The lesions expand rapidly, and the leaf becomes completely dead. White spores are seen on leaves.

llama.raw_text: Affected leaves turn reddish brown and bronzy. Severe infestation leaves silken webbing on the leaves, wither and dry. Flower and fruit formation are affected. Field sanitation: remove affected plants. Plant tall border crops like maize or sorghum. Spray thoroughly on the underside of the leaves.

llama.raw_text: Yellow blotches with a yellow halo appear on leaves. Abundant white spores are found in the infected area. Plant tomatoes 3 feet apart to allow for good air circulation. Mulch around the plants to protect the roots.
llama.text: Yellow blotches with a yellow halo appear on leaves. Abundant white spores are found in the infected area. Plant tomatoes 3 feet apart to allow for good air circulation. Mulch around the plants to protect the roots.

llama.raw_text: Symptoms only appear on the leaves. The leaves will soon fall off after infection. No discoloration was seen on the upper side of the leaves. Burn the infected leaves.
llama.text: Symptoms only appear on the leaves. The leaves will soon fall off after infection. No discoloration was seen on the upper side of the leaves. Burn the infected leaves.

llama.raw_text: Root-knot nematodes cause root galls on the feeder roots and sometimes affect the entire root system, showing heavy galling. Infected plants appear in patches in the field. Roots branch profusely from the gall tissue, causing a 'beard root' symptom.

llama.raw_text: Small, round to irregular spots with a grey centre and dark margin on leaves. Spots join and leaves are blighted; complete defoliation. Stems and flowers are also affected.

llama.raw_text: Leaves with serpentine mines drop off. The tiny, metallic fly punctures the leaf and feeds on the sap. Typical serpentine shaped tunnels are formed in the leaf.

llama.raw_text: Young larvae eat leaves on the underside of the leaf.

llama.raw_text: Thrips suck the sap from tomato plants. Use locally available empty tins painted blue and coated with grease, vaseline, or castor oil as an alternative trap. Plant 5-6 rows of sorghum or maize around the field as a barrier crop.

llama.raw_text: Mottling on leaves with wilting of young leaves in sunny days. The leaflets are distorted, puckered, and smaller than normal. The affected plant is stunted, pale green, and spindly.

llama.raw_text: Severe stunting. Chlorotic or necrotic rings form on the leaves of many infected hosts. Growing tips may die-back and terminal branches may be streaked. Use healthy seedlings for transplanting. Plant sorghum, maize, or bajra as a barrier crop.

llama.raw_text: Destroy the plants and fruits that are infested with the pinworm. Use healthy seedlings when transplanting tomatoes.

llama.raw_text: Whitefly is a vector that spreads tomato leaf curl disease. Whitefly has a mouthpart that pierces and sucks the sap from leaves.

llama.raw_text: Whiteflies spread the virus. Choose healthy seedlings. Remove and destroy infected plants.
